deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. This page continues Gauss's trigonometric levelling of the Hannover arc measurement. The previous page gives the 1821–23 table of arcs, refractions and the absolute heights relative to the Göttingen Sternwarte. It is labelled 'Abgedruckt im Astr. Jahrb. für 1826'. The page has three parts: (A) reduction of reciprocal elevation angles from the 1824 Lüneburg/Hamburg stations; (B) an update of the mean refraction coefficient; (C) a least-squares adjustment of the 17-station height network with its mean error.

(A) RECIPROCAL LEVELLING. There are five station pairs: Wilsede–Lüneburg, Nindorf–Lüneburg, Wilsede–Hamburg, Timpenberg–Hamburg and Nindorf–Hamburg. The columns are as follows.
- Col. 1: centring offsets (metres), sometimes two, one per observing series.
- Col. 2: the same offsets turned into seconds by dividing by the distance r. Checks: 2.067/0.322 = 131.509/20.488 = 6.419 ⇒ r ≈ 32 130 m, and log r = 4.50697; 126.669/26.076 = 74.012/15.236 = 4.858 ⇒ r ≈ 42 460 m, and log r = 4.62800.
- Col. 3: observed elevation angles.
- Col. 4: reduced angle α (in seconds). It is angle + correction; when there are two series it is their mean. Example: Wilsede gives ½[(−1054.150+2.067)+(−911.075−131.509)] = −1047.333.
- Col. 5 (first line of each pair): height difference by the formula on the previous page, Δh = ½(α−α′)·r·(sec α sec α′)^{1/3}·(1+(h+h′)/2R). Checks: ½(−621.585+735.975)″·49 108 m = +13.617 (Gauss +13.614); Wilsede–Hamburg gives −41.960 (Gauss −41.959).
- Col. 5 (second line): the arc θ = r/R in seconds.
- Col. 6: total refraction ρ = θ + α + α′. Example: 445.411 − 798.798 + 400.804 = 47.417.
- Col. 7: log r over the ratio ρ/θ. Example: 47.417/445.411 = 0.1065.

The values for Hamburg are not entered in the adjustment. Gauss's adopted Hamburg height (−26.693, last row of the list) agrees with the mean of three determinations (my reconstruction):
- 14.876 − 41.959 = −27.083
- −39.026 + 11.395 = −27.631
- −38.978 + 13.614 = −25.364
- Mean (−27.083 − 27.631 − 25.364)/3 = −26.693.

(B) REFRACTION. The '6 ersten Bögen' are the four 1823 pairs from the previous page (197.632, 731.300, 749.222, 99.935) plus the two Lüneburg pairs (1037.476, 445.411).
- Σθ = 3260.976″ and Σρ = 14.651 + 77.074 + 76.906 − 9.941 + 147.576 + 47.417 = 353.683 ≈ 353.684, giving ratio 0.1085.
- Adding the 1821–23 totals (33233.273 and 4309.986) gives 36494.249 and 4663.670, so the ratio is 0.12779. This is the coefficient of total (two-ended) refraction; the one-ended coefficient is k ≈ 0.0639.
- Marginal notes (probably Krüger's, 'Kr') refer to p. 72 and to a letter to Schumacher of 28 Nov 1824.

(C) LEAST-SQUARES HEIGHT ADJUSTMENT.
- Stations are numbered 1 = Sternwarte, 2 Meridianzeichen, 3 Hohehagen, 4 Hils, 5 Brocken, 6 Lichtenberg, 7 Deister, 8 Garssen, 9 Falkenberg, 10 Scharnhorst, 11 Breithorn, 12 Hauselberg, 13 Wilsede, 14 Wulfsode, 15 Timpenberg, 16 Nindorf, 17 Lüneburg.
- Height 1 is held at 0. The 16 unknowns a,b,c,d,e,f,g,h,i,k,l,m,n,o,p,q (no j) are corrections to the height differences along a spanning tree: 1–2 a, 2–3 b, 2–4 c, 4–5 d, 4–6 e, 4–7 f, 7–8 g, 7–9 h, 9–10 i, 9–11 k, 9–12 l, 9–13 m, 13–14 n, 13–15 o, 13–16 p, 13–17 q.
- Each station correction is the sum of the tree edges from station 1; for example Wilsede gets a+c+f+h+m.
- For each of the 34 observed differences O_ij, the residual is v = (H_j⁰ − H_i⁰ − O_ij) + (X_j − X_i), where H⁰ are the provisional heights. Example: 1.3 gives 348.424 − 349.366 = −0.942, plus a+b.
- Forming Σ(∂v/∂x)·v = 0 gives 16 normal equations, all with unit weights. The coefficient matrix is the reduced graph Laplacian; for example the a-row is 2a + b and the m-row is −k − 2l + 5m + 2n.
- The absolute terms are all 0, ±0.001 or ±0.002. So the provisional heights are already the least-squares solution to rounding, and the page is effectively a verification of them.
- Then Σvv = 34.167477, n − u = 34 − 16 = 18, Σvv/18 = 1.898193 and √ = 1.37775. This is the mean error of one observed height difference, ≈ ±1.38 m, using the n − u divisor of Theoria Combinationis (1823).
errors: Wilsede–Lüneburg refraction: θ+α+α′ = 1037.476 − 1047.333 + 157.633 = 147.776, but Gauss writes 147.576 (a 0.2″ slip). It propagates into ratio 0.1422 (should be 0.1424) and Σρ = 353.684 (should be 353.884). Mean ratios 0.1085 and 0.12779 change only in the 4th–5th digit (0.10852, 0.12780).

Nindorf–Lüneburg: the Lüneburg angle as read (+6′37.863″) plus 22.940 gives 420.803, not 400.804. The written 400.804, the refraction 47.417 and Δh all require +6′17.863″, so this is either a slip in the angle or a misreading.
Nindorf–Hamburg: −12′14.827″ − 1.168 = −735.995, Gauss writes −735.975 (0.02″). His refraction 229.263 uses the written value.

Wilsede–Hamburg: the mean of the two corrected series as read, ½[(−914.375+126.669)+(−716.500−74.012)], is −789.109, not −789.577. Either a slip or a misread digit; it does not affect the Hamburg mean beyond ≈0.02 m.

Timpenberg–Hamburg: ½(−667.455+758.592)″·r with log r = 4.71055 gives ≈ +11.34 m, versus Gauss's +11.395. The discrepancy may be a slip, or there may be an unrecorded height reduction; I am uncertain.

Normal equations for o and p: observation 15.16 enters as (−o+p), so the off-diagonal coupling must be −1. The o-row should read −n+3o−p and the p-row −o+3p−q. The manuscript appears to show +p and +o. This is harmless because all absolute terms are ≈0.
Σvv recomputed from the 34 written residuals is 34.167459 against Gauss's 34.167477 (a difference of 1.8e−5). This is negligible and the mean error 1.37775 is unaffected.

results.what: Reciprocal trigonometric levelling with centring reductions, the height formula Δh = ½(α−α′) r (sec α sec α′)^{1/3}(1+(h+h′)/2R), and the refraction coefficient as total refraction/arc
results.modern_name: Reciprocal trigonometric levelling; terrestrial refraction coefficient k (here 2k ≈ 0.128)
results.usually_credited_to: Standard geodesy; Gauss's coefficient k ≈ 0.0653 from the Hannover survey is classical (Gauss 1823/1826)

results.what: Least-squares adjustment of a levelling network by parameters, with corrections parametrised along a spanning tree and normal equations equal to the reduced graph Laplacian
results.modern_name: Adjustment of indirect observations (Gauss–Markov model) for a levelling network

results.what: Mean error of unit weight from √(Σvv/(n−u)) with n = 34 and u = 16
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss, Theoria Combinationis Observationum, pars posterior (1823)

results.what: Height of Hamburg taken as the mean of three independent determinations (from Wilsede, Timpenberg and Nindorf)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine working page of Gauss's 1824 extension of the Hannover levelling. The least-squares network adjustment, the n−u mean error and the refraction coefficient are all Gauss's own published methods (1821–1826). It is a nice concrete application, but nothing here goes beyond what is known to be his.
